title: Coverage Updates and Rebilling on the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing)
content:
A patient who reports insurance that was active on the date of service, after the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account was billed as self-pay or to a different payer, has the coverage verified while the account may sit on a coverage-update-pending hold.

## When newly reported coverage is billed

Newly reported coverage is billed only when both hold:

1. it is reported within the coverage-update window of the first statement date; and
2. the payer's own timely-filing limit, counted from the date of service, has not expired.

| Reported within the window | Payer's limit expired | Result |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no | financial class updated and the account rebilled |
| yes | yes | not rebilled; the self-pay balance stands |
| no | either | not billed to the newly reported coverage |

## The rebill

When both hold, the financial class is updated and the account is rebilled: the open self-pay balance net of the uninsured discount and of patient payments is transferred off the patient balance as an insurance rebill transfer adjustment, and a new claim is submitted. Payments already made remain on the account and are reconciled when the payer adjudicates.

## Terminated coverage

Coverage reported as terminated before the date of service changes the financial class to self-pay, and the payer's denial amount posts as coverage-terminated liability.

*Illustration (hypothetical).* A self-pay account with gross liability 1000.00, an uninsured discount of 400.00 and a patient payment of 100.00 transfers 500.00 off the patient balance on rebill; the 100.00 payment stays on the account.
